front: What is Cilium in one sentence?

back: Pod eth0 ──► veth ──► node eBPF (Cilium) ──► cluster routing / encap → kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l k8s-app=cilium → cilium status --wait # cilium CLI on node or debug pod → kubectl -n kube-system exec ds/cilium -- cilium status → helm upgrade cilium cilium/cilium -n kube-system --set hubble.enabled=true \

front: Symptom: Pod ContainerCreating stuck — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: kubectl describe pod; Cilium IPAM events · Fix: Free CIDR; fix IPAM mode; restart agent

front: Symptom: Service unreachable — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: cilium service list; endpoints · Fix: Missing backend pods; wrong selector; BPF LB disabled

front: Symptom: Policy suddenly blocks traffic — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: hubble observe --verdict DROPPED · Fix: Label mismatch; namespace selector; add explicit allow

front: Symptom: DNS timeouts — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Hubble to kube-dns; CoreDNS policy · Fix: Allow udp/53 to kube-system; Cilium DNS policy

front: Symptom: NodeNotReady after upgrade — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: cilium status; kernel ≥ requirement · Fix: Match Cilium version matrix; eBPF modules loaded

front: Symptom: Cross-node pod fail — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Encapsulation: VXLAN/GENEVE vs routing · Fix: Native routing needs L2 adjacency; fix underlay MTU

front: Symptom: High CPU on cilium-agent — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Map pressure, policy count · Fix: Split policies; upgrade; reduce L7 scope

front: Symptom: Works with NP disabled — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Confirm with kubectl get netpol · Fix: Default deny + explicit allows in zero-trust

front: Gotcha with Cilium: what silently fails?
back: NetworkPolicy default allow — K8s without NP = all pods talk. Adding first deny-all without allow rules = outage.

front: When should you NOT use Cilium?
back: Tiny single-node lab — flannel/canal simpler; Cilium shines at policy + observability scale. Non-Kubernetes bare metal — Cilium exists but different install; don't assume kube chart. Replacing app auth with NP — network segmentation complements, doesn't replace mTLS/authZ.

front: What is ingress in one sentence?
back: HTTP/S routing into the cluster — Ingress = rules; Ingress Controller = program that implements them — Kubernetes: Up and Running (Burns et al.).

front: Explain the mental model of ingress (how the system thinks).
back: Ingress resource alone does nothing — you must install a controller Deployment + class.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for ingress?
back: Internet ──► LB / NodePort ──► Ingress Controller (nginx, traefik, cilium, ALB…) → Ingress spec.rules[].host + path ──maps──► Service.name:port ──► Pod endpoints → kubectl get ingressclass

front: Given a broken ingress setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Internet ──► LB / NodePort ──► Ingress Controller (nginx, traefik, cilium, ALB…)

front: Symptom: 404 from ingress — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: host/path rule mismatch · Fix: Add rule; check pathType Prefix vs Exact

front: Symptom: 503 Service Unavailable — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: endpoints empty · Fix: Fix readiness; pod crash — kubectl CrashLoop

front: Symptom: 502 intermittent — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: controller + app logs · Fix: Timeouts; pod restarts; HPA flapping

front: Symptom: 525/526 SSL (CF) — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: origin cert · Fix: Full chain in secret tls.crt; SNI host match

front: Symptom: Wrong backend — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: multiple Ingress same host · Fix: Rule precedence; merge order

front: Symptom: Works via port-forward, not ingress — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Service selector · Fix: Labels; different namespace

front: Symptom: Infinite redirect — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: http→https loop · Fix: ssl-redirect + backend HTTP scheme

front: Gotcha with ingress: what silently fails?
back: Ingress without IngressClass — ignored on 1.18+ clusters; silent "nothing happens."

front: When should you NOT use ingress?
back: Non-HTTP TCP services — use Service type=LoadBalancer or Gateway API TCPRoute. Internal-only east-west — ClusterIP Service directly; no ingress hop. Mesh mTLS replaces ingress TLS — still need edge termination for public clients.

front: What is kubectl pod creation in one sentence?
back: Ship a Pod object through the API — imperative one-offs, declarative manifests, or generated YAML — Kubernetes: Up and Running (Burns et al.) + The Kubernetes Book (Sayed).

front: What is restartPolicy?
back: Always (default), OnFailure, Never. For Jobs/CronJobs use OnFailure or Never; Deployments ignore this on the Pod template (always Always).

front: What is resources.requests?
back: scheduler uses these for placement; omit → BestEffort QoS → first evicted under pressure.

front: What is resources.limits?
back: cgroup cap; OOM kills container when exceeded.

front: What is Probes?
back: readiness keeps bad pods out of Service endpoints; liveness restarts stuck containers.

front: Explain the mental model of kubectl pod creation (how the system thinks).
back: A Pod is the smallest deployable unit: one or more containers that share network and optional volumes. kubectl does not “run a container” on a node directly — it creates a Pod API object; controllers and kubelet do the rest.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for kubectl pod creation?
back: kubectl run / apply ──► kube-apiserver ──► etcd (Pod desired state) → scheduler assigns node → kubelet starts containers on that node → Annotate the knobs: → Sidecars share the Pod IP and can use localhost; they must not bind the same containerPort.

front: Symptom: Forbidden / RBAC error — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: kubectl auth can-i create pods -n prod · Fix: Grant create pods; check RoleBinding

front: Symptom: AlreadyExists — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: kubectl get pod -n prod <name> · Fix: Delete old pod, rename, or use apply

front: Symptom: Stuck Pending — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: kubectl describe pod → Events · Fix: Taints/tolerations; insufficient CPU/mem; PVC not bound

front: Symptom: ImagePullBackOff — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: describe → Failed to pull · Fix: Wrong tag; private registry → imagePullSecrets

front: Symptom: CreateContainerConfigError — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: describe → secret/configmap not found · Fix: Create Secret/ConfigMap; fix key name

front: Symptom: CrashLoopBackOff right after create — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: kubectl logs --previous · Fix: Bad command; missing env; probe too aggressive → kubectl

front: Symptom: Pod created but no Service traffic — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: kubectl get endpoints · Fix: Pod not Ready; labels don’t match Service selector → Kubernetes services

front: Symptom: Changes to YAML ignored — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: kubectl get pod -o yaml vs file · Fix: Bare Pod is mostly immutable — delete and recreate, or use Deployment

front: Gotcha with kubectl pod creation: what silently fails?
back: Standalone Pods are not recreated — kubelet restarts containers per restartPolicy, but if the Pod object is deleted or the node dies, nothing brings it back. Use Deployment/StatefulSet for long-lived apps.

front: When should you NOT use kubectl pod creation?
back: Production app tiers — create a Deployment (or StatefulSet) instead; bare Pod creation is for debug, Jobs, or operator-managed objects. Replacing GitOps — manual kubectl run in prod drifts from Argo/Flux source; fix the repo. Scaling — bare Pods don’t scale; use Deployment replicas or HPA.
